title: Voting (2 out of 3)
goals: See how the three calculation methods differ and when the approximations are safe.
assumptions: A, B and C fail independently with a made-up probability of 0.1 each. Nothing here describes a real plant.

steps.prompt: Add three basic events named A, B and C, each with probability 0.1.
steps.hint: The system fails if at least two of the three fail. Name each event in the Name field; the lesson finds your events by their names.

steps.prompt: Add a voting gate that fails when at least 2 of A, B, C fail. Make it the top event and run with each method.
steps.hint: Use the K-of-N gate button and set K to 2. The gate then fails when at least 2 of its 3 inputs fail.

mistakes.message: A probability above 1 is not allowed. Write 10 percent as 0.1.
The top gate is not a voting gate. AND needs all three to fail and OR needs only one.

hand_calculation: Rare-event: add the three cut sets, 3 x 0.01 = 0.03. It is above the exact value because it counts overlaps twice.
Min-cut upper bound: 1 - (1 - 0.01)^3 = 0.029701. Both approximations are close when probabilities are small and drift apart as they grow.
